system: You are an ambitious AI PhD student in computational mathematics who is looking to publish a paper that will contribute significantly to the field.
task_description: You are given the following file to work with, which implements a symbolic law discovery harness: it searches over symbolic expression trees to recover hidden closed-form mathematical laws (drawn from physics and mathematics) from sampled data. A candidate law is scored by normalized RMSE after fitting a single multiplicative constant, and any candidate that fits to high precision is additionally verified *symbolically* with sympy, i.e. proven equal to the ground truth up to a constant factor rather than merely fitting numerically. The baseline search strategy in `propose_candidate` is deliberately naive uniform random search over expression trees. Your goal is to invent and evaluate new mathematical search techniques that discover more laws, discover them in fewer candidate evaluations, or discover simpler (lower-complexity) verified forms: for example evolutionary or annealing-based tree search, exploiting the evaluation history, complexity-guided or Pareto-based selection, algebraic canonicalization to avoid re-evaluating equivalent expressions, dimensional-analysis-style pruning, decomposition of the problem into sub-laws, or improved constant-fitting and verification procedures. Experiments run on CPU in a few minutes; you may not add new datasets or external dependencies beyond numpy and sympy, and results must remain deterministic given the seeds.
